entries.why: Attribution on DISCOVERY (H1 look20 buf0.0 atr1 hold12, 6,678 trades) showed stop-hit trades are 56.4% of the book and account for -4,066.6R, while full-hold time exits earn +2.5212R each. Losers reached only 0.726R MFE before dying at 1.407R MAE, i.e. they were killed while still near entry, not after a real move against them.
entries.change: Same signal rule, same hold, same session deadline, same cost. Stop moves from 1x ATR to 2x ATR. R is renormalised to the new risk, so E(R) stays comparable under fixed-fractional sizing.
entries.criterion: Paired per-signal difference (variant minus baseline on signals BOTH arms take) must beat the declared margin, and its block-bootstrap t must clear the cumulative-k floor.
entries.test_period: HOLDOUT H1 2017-01-01 onwards - the attribution that suggested this ran on discovery only

result.note: Win rate rose 33.4%->44.0% and 3,601 of 5,455 signals improved against 1,854 worsened, yet the net is +0.0010R. The wider stop converts many small losses into small wins and makes the remaining losses proportionally larger; the money nets out. Separately: the baseline itself earns -0.0001R on holdout against +0.0175R on discovery, so the config being improved has no edge to improve.

entries.why: Arithmetic, not a pattern: the spread is fixed at 0.260 price units regardless of horizon, so the only way to raise the gross edge against it is a larger move. The first test proved the stop cannot do this - it scales the edge and the cost by the same factor. Hold is the other lever. DISCLOSURE: I have already seen the holdout cost decomposition for atr1/atr2, so this test is not fully blind. Recorded here rather than hidden.
entries.change: Same signal rule, same atr1 stop, same session deadline, same cost. hold_max moves from 12 bars to 24. The 20:30 UTC force-close still binds first on most trades, so the effective change is smaller than 12 to 24 suggests.
entries.criterion: Paired per-signal difference on shared signals must beat the declared margin, and its block-bootstrap t must clear the cumulative-k floor.

result.note: The session deadline binds first: 4,886 of 5,455 trades were UNCHANGED because the 20:30 UTC force-close already closed them before bar 12. Of the 569 that could move, 255 improved and 314 worsened. The horizon lever is not available on an intraday setup - rule 6 (force close before rollover) caps it structurally, so raising hold_max on H1 changes almost nothing and what it does change is slightly worse.

entries.why: User's argument: one strict setup firing once a month is unmeasurable, but 100 equally strict setups reach 70+ signals a month, which IS tradeable. Acknowledged upfront that it would be overfit, but proposed the result might still be positive. The frequency half of this is correct and setup_power.py answered the wrong question by treating one setup in isolation.
entries.change: Take the frozen 176-cell grid in multi_tf_setup_grid.py WHOLE (11 entry families x params x 4 exits x 2 stops). Select cells on DISCOVERY only by six declared rules, then measure those same cells on HOLDOUT as one pooled portfolio, block-bootstrapped over time so cross-cell overlap is carried, and against a matched control that preserves direction mix and exit design but randomises entry timing.
entries.criterion: The pooled holdout book must beat zero with a block-bootstrap t clearing the floor for the number of selection rules tried, AND show skill over the timing-destroyed control.
entries.test_period: HOLDOUT H1 2017-01-01 onwards; selection used DISCOVERY 2004-2017 only

result.note: Best rule was keep-t>2: 28 cells, holdout E +0.0269R. Baseline here is the matched control (+0.0029) since the question is entry skill, not raw return. Naive t was +3.12 but collapsed to +1.00 once cross-cell overlap was carried - 28 cells trading the same gold on the same bars are not 28 independent samples. Skill over the timing-destroyed control is +0.0240 at block t +0.90. NOT flat zero the way pure selection is (Part 1 null gives 0.0000 regardless of strictness), so something is carried from discovery to holdout - but it is indistinguishable from noise and 57% of the selected cells are Donchian breakout, the family cross_market.py independently closed on 9 of 9 markets.

entries.why: User's refinement: do not loosen the rare setup - make it STRICTER still, and run enough strict setups to reach 60 signals a month. The existing four-stage ablation supports the premise: E rises monotonically with depth (-0.091, +0.001, +0.039, +0.296) and the stated reason row 4 is not a result is that its MDE exceeds its effect, which is a SAMPLE SIZE objection that breadth legitimately answers.
entries.change: Build conjunctions BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by selection: every combination of k conditions from a fixed 13-condition library, depths 1 to 4, nothing dropped for looking bad or for being rare. Pool all trades at each depth. Compare against two nulls - time-shuffled conditions (same rarity, no information) and randomised timing (same directions, same drift, no timing claim).
entries.criterion: Skill over the timing control must RISE with depth and clear the floor for the number of depths tried.

result.note: Baseline is depth 1 skill, variant is depth 4 skill - the question was whether strictness RAISES skill. It does not: skill runs +0.0200, +0.0206, +0.0261, +0.0159 across depths 1-4, flat and never significant (t +0.77, +0.61, +0.63, +0.33 against a 1.67 floor). Raw E does rise (+0.0218 to +0.0544) and time-shuffled conditions do NOT reproduce that rise - but the randomised-TIMING control does, rising +0.0017 to +0.0384. So the rise is a sampling-density effect of sparse signals, not information in the conditions. Separately, every depth's skill is below the 0.0518R round-trip cost at a 1.5 ATR stop.

entries.why: combinatorics.py measured that the 131,040-cell nominal space is only of order 751 effectively independent questions (m_eff = 3.69 k^0.451, fitted on measured return-series correlation). So the whole space can be probed at 751 tests rather than 131,040, and the honest multiple-testing floor is sqrt(2 ln 751) = 3.64 rather than 4.85. Running the representatives is cheap and the floor is already known.
entries.change: Stratified random sample of 751 cells across depth 1-6 x 4 exits x 2 stops x 4 timeframes, seed 17 fixed and declared. NOTHING is chosen by performance - the strata and the seed fully determine the sample. Each cell measured on its own timeframe's discovery split, then the same cell measured on holdout. Skill is taken against a randomised-TIMING control, not raw E, because strictness.py showed raw E carries a signal-density artefact that a random-timing book reproduces.
entries.criterion: A cell PASSES only if its discovery skill t clears 3.64 AND its holdout skill is positive. Both, declared now. The pooled all-751 book is reported alongside as the no-selection baseline.
entries.test_period: Per timeframe: H1 discovery 2004-2017 / holdout 2017-2026; M5-M30 discovery to 2023 / holdout 2023-2026

result.note: 324 of 751 cells produced a usable book on both periods. Distribution of discovery skill t is OVER-DISPERSED (mean +0.155, sd 1.475 against noise 0 and 1; max +4.66, min -5.79) so the space is not dead - but the dispersion is symmetric, the signature of effects strong within a period and reversing between them. 3 cells cleared the 3.64 floor on discovery, 1 was also positive on holdout: fast_ema+in_fvg+mom_50 on H1 trail-2ATR-BE, discovery skill +0.1214 t+4.66, holdout skill +0.0265 t+0.87. Decisive number is the rank test: corr(discovery t, holdout skill) over 318 cells is Pearson -0.016 (-0.3 SE) and Spearman +0.102 (+1.8 SE), neither clearing 2 SE, and the WORST discovery quintile has higher mean holdout skill (+0.0166) than the best (+0.0042). No-selection baseline is E -0.0707 discovery, -0.0502 holdout.

entries.why: Four commercial KRV EAs supplied as compiled .ex5 (no source, high entropy, no readable logic). The EAs themselves cannot be read, but the four FAMILIES their names describe can each be implemented from a standard textbook definition and tested. A dead family is strong evidence against any implementation of it; a live family would justify asking the vendor for the .mq5.
entries.change: Implement four families from standard definitions: (1) regular price/RSI divergence reversal, (2) range compression then breakout of the compressed range, (3) exhaustion reversal after an extended run plus a climax bar, (4) tick-volume profile POC/value-area zones. Each at 3 declared parameter variants x 2 exit designs. Skill measured against a randomised-timing control. Discovery then holdout, block-bootstrapped.
entries.criterion: A family survives only if at least one variant clears the floor for 24 tests on DISCOVERY and keeps positive skill on HOLDOUT, and its skill exceeds the round-trip cost.

result.note: All four families fail the registered three-part criterion. Best is compression (n=12,q=0.20, stop+time): discovery skill +0.3624 at t+3.61, clears the 2.52 floor, but holdout skill collapses to +0.0423 at t+0.41 - BELOW the 0.0518R round-trip cost, so baseline here is the cost itself. Compression is coherent on discovery (3 of 6 variants above t+3.0) and gone on holdout (+0.0423, +0.0241, +0.0173, -0.0156, -0.0124, -0.1490). divergence best t_d +1.42, exhaustion best t_d -0.24 (negative skill on every variant), volume_poc best t_d +2.51 - none clears. NOTE: these are reimplementations from the family names, NOT tests of the compiled .ex5 binaries, whose logic is unrecoverable. Evidence runs one way only: dead family is evidence against any build of it; a live one would only justify requesting the .mq5.

entries.why: The vendor supplied full written specifications for all four EAs. My first implementation (vendor_four_families, REJECTED) was materially wrong against those specs: Volume Power Zones is a volume-weighted ORDER BLOCK with an ATR-x4 displacement trigger and a retest, not a volume profile POC - I implemented the wrong strategy entirely. Exhaustion omitted its core mechanism, declining volume through the run plus a shift bar on ABOVE-average volume. Divergence omitted Hidden divergence and every trend filter, which the docs single out as the biggest win-rate lever. Compression omitted BBW, the minimum squeeze duration, the impulse-body test and the volume surge. The previous REJECTED verdict therefore does not stand as a test of these families.
entries.change: Reimplement all four to the written specs. Divergence: Regular AND Hidden, with and without an HTF EMA trend gate. Compression: BBW and ATR both below their own rolling means for a minimum number of bars, range box, close breakout plus impulse body, with and without volume surge. Exhaustion: 4-9 bar run with declining relative volume, then an opposite shift bar on above-average volume with a body-ratio and close-position test. Volume Power Zones: confirmed swing pivots weighted by volume against a 20-bar volume MA, ATR-x4 displacement trigger, retest of the block with a cooldown. 10 signal configurations x 2 exits.
entries.criterion: A family survives only if at least one configuration clears the floor for 20 tests on DISCOVERY, keeps positive skill on HOLDOUT, and its holdout skill exceeds the round-trip cost. All three, as before.

result.note: ONE configuration meets the registered three-part criterion: compression, min_bars=6 impulse=1.0 vol_surge=True, 1leg 2R BE. Discovery skill +0.1564 at t+3.58 (clears the 2.52 floor, 1,023 trades); holdout skill +0.0999 at t+1.93 (positive, and above the 0.0518R cost, 785 trades). Baseline here is the cost itself. The volume surge is what did it and it is a filter from the vendor's own documentation, not something searched for: without it t_d +2.63/+1.36 and holdout -0.0701/-0.0471; with it t_d +3.58/+4.07 and holdout +0.0999/-0.0073. Caveats: 1 of 24 tests, holdout t does not itself clear the floor, and the 3leg sister config of the same signal is negative on holdout. Ran 24 tests not the 20 registered (12 configs x 2 exits, not 10) - floor 2.52 rather than 2.45, stricter than registered. Everything else dead: div_regular best t_d +2.49, div_hidden +0.65, exhaustion +2.05, power_zones +0.89.

entries.why: One configuration cleared all three parts of the vendor_families_v2 criterion: compression with vol_surge=True at 1leg 2R BE, discovery skill +0.1564 t+3.58, holdout skill +0.0999 t+1.93 against a 0.0518R cost. The volume surge is the vendor's own documented filter, not a searched parameter, and turning it on flipped holdout from -0.0701 to +0.0999. It is still 1 of 24 tests on one instrument, and this repo's standing rule is that an effect found on gold and absent elsewhere is gold overfit.
entries.change: Freeze that exact rule - BBW and ATR both under their rolling means for 6 bars, range box, close breakout with body >= 1.0 ATR, volume above 1.2x its 20-bar mean, 1.5 ATR stop, single 2R target with break-even - and run it unchanged on all nine markets, each charged its own measured median spread. No parameter is refitted per market. For the eight non-gold markets every bar is out of sample, since none of their data was used to find the rule.
entries.criterion: Pre-declared at the same bar cross_market.py already uses: the rule REPLICATES only if skill is positive on at least 8 of 9 markets (binomial P = 1.95%). 7 of 9 is suggestive and is NOT a pass. Markets are not independent, so the binomial figure is an upper bound on the evidence.

result.note: REPLICATES at the pre-declared bar: positive skill on 8 of 9 markets, P=0.0195 (t recorded is the binomial-equivalent z of 2.06). Mean skill +0.0333, median +0.0364, four markets at t>2 (gold +2.78, EURUSD +2.68, USDJPY +2.42, GBPUSD +2.12). The eight non-gold markets are out of sample in every respect and are positive on 7 of 8. This is the first rule in the project to replicate cross-market. BUT SKILL IS NOT PROFIT and here they come apart: E(R) is positive on only 2 of 9 (EURUSD +0.0137 at t+0.42, USDJPY +0.0235 at t+0.64) and NOTHING is significantly profitable anywhere. The cost relationship is real - slope -1.5070, and it survives removing XAGUSD (slope -0.5983) - but the zero-cost intercept falls from +0.0759 to +0.0143 once silver is dropped, so most of the apparent gross edge was that one point. +0.0143 is indistinguishable from zero. Reading: the entry carries genuine information about timing, replicated across nine markets, and not enough of it to pay a spread anywhere.

entries.why: HONESTLY NOT BLIND: found via debugging the vendor's 25-template spec (xauusd_1000_setups.py). P01 (Donchian-20 breakout) on M15 2019-2026 real bid/ask cleared the baseline floor after a control-bug fix, and is the SAME family cross_market.py already declared dead 9/9 markets under a different spec (SL=1.5xATR, TP=2R, 12-bar hold, flat 260pt cost). This spec differs materially: SL from the signal bar's own low/high + buffer, TP=1R, 24-bar hold, REAL bid/ask fill (Buy@Ask/Sell@Bid) instead of mid minus a flat spread. Extended to full H1 2004-2026 it gave discovery skill +0.1094 t+3.70, holdout skill +0.1046 t+4.42, both periods gross E(R) positive (+0.0538, +0.0856). That is the best number this project has ever produced if real, and results this good after this many dead ends are the ones most likely to hide a bug - which is exactly why this is registered before being trusted rather than reported.
entries.change: Freeze the P01 spec exactly (Donchian-20 breakout, TP=1R from real fill, SL=bar low/high minus buffer, 24-bar time exit, tick-rounded, G09 pre-trade gate) and run it unchanged, real bid/ask, on all 9 markets this repo has H1 bid/ask for. No refitting per market.
entries.criterion: Same bar as every prior cross-market test in this project: skill positive on at least 8 of 9 markets (binomial P=1.95%), AND gross E(R) positive on at least 6 of 9 (since this project's standing lesson is that skill and profit are different claims and skill alone was not enough for the compression rule).

result.note: RETRACTED BY ITS OWN CALIBRATION. The pre-fix run met both halves of the declared criterion spectacularly: skill positive 9 of 9 on both periods (P=0.0020), gross E(R) positive 9 of 9, t up to +9.68. It was a one-bar look-ahead. Entry used ask_CLOSE of bar t+1 while the exit loop scanned that same bar's high and low, so trades could be resolved by price action that happened before they were entered; the spec says 'Ask แรกของแท่ง t+1' - the OPEN. Caught by running the rule on mega_search.synth martingale data, where a correct engine must return skill 0 and E(R) = minus the spread: it returned skill +0.0728 (t up to +5.02) and E(R) +0.0034. After the fix the same synthetic calibration returns skill +0.0016 and E(R) -0.0590, and the nine real markets collapse to skill positive 5 of 9 (a coin flip), gross E(R) positive 0 of 9, mean E(R) -0.0652. Two further real fixes were made in the same pass: exits were tested against MID highs and lows while entries filled at the real ask, charging half a spread instead of a whole one; and the random-timing control used a fixed 1.5xATR stop against a rule whose stop ranges 0.3-3 ATR, so R had different denominators in the two books. Neither of those was the main defect. The 13-template M15 baseline re-run with the fixed engine has 0 of 13 clearing the floor.

entries.why: README marks Setup D as the ONE hypothesis that survived this project's own 16-round research: (Close-SMA200)/ATR in [1.08,7.21], permutation p=0.0005, net E +0.2312R at 8R. It is the EA's only default-ON setup. Config.mqh states plainly 'NOT YET VALIDATED: the zone was found on the FULL gold sample, not a held-out half, and cross-asset confirmation (silver, EURUSD) has not been run. If it does not reproduce there, this is gold overfit.' That test has never been run. Separately, the README's own drift table shows longs-in-zone skill is NEGATIVE after subtracting drift (-0.0494, t-4.14) while the default config trades ONLY longs - so the side being traded is the side whose raw edge is drift.
entries.change: Implement Setup D exactly: z=(Close-SMA200)/ATR, long [1.08,7.21] short [-7.21,-1.08], fire only on ENTERING the zone, flat 1.8 ATR stop, 8R target, 30-hour time stop, one position at a time, real bid/ask fill at the entry bar's open quote. Two runs: (1) gold M15 to verify the implementation reproduces the documented result before anything else is believed, (2) all 9 markets on H1 with the time stop matched in wall-clock hours. Report raw E AND drift-adjusted skill per market per side.
entries.criterion: Cross-asset validation as Config.mqh itself defines it: the zone must reproduce outside gold. Declared bar - DRIFT-ADJUSTED skill positive on at least 8 of 9 markets for whichever side is traded (binomial P=1.95%), AND the gold M15 verification run must land within a factor of two of the documented +0.2312R at 8R, otherwise the implementation is wrong and nothing else in the run counts.
entries.test_period: gold M15 2019-2026 for verification; 9 markets H1 2004-2026 for cross-asset

result.note: Does NOT replicate. Drift-adjusted skill positive on 0 of 9 markets on BOTH sides (declared bar was 8 of 9 on the long side). Long mean skill -0.1322 (across-market t -2.97), short -0.1226 (t -3.51). Only USDJPY long had positive raw E (+0.0557) and its skill was -0.0535 - the market went up, measured twice. Gold itself is in the failing set: XAUUSD H1 long E -0.0994, skill -0.1055. Implementation verified first: gold M15 reproduces +0.1788R at zero cost against the documented +0.2312R (which README's own table says was costed at the $0.26 terminal quote), within the declared factor of two; at real measured bid/ask the same book is +0.0439R. So the gap is cost, not a coding error, and the nine-market result is a genuine test. This is exactly the outcome Config.mqh warned about. Note also that README's own drift table already showed the long side - the ONLY side the shipped config trades - has NEGATIVE drift-adjusted skill on gold itself (-0.0494, t -4.14), while the side with positive skill (shorts, +0.1092, t +7.56) is switched off.

entries.why: Every test in this repo - 33 topics, 40 files - runs at M1 to H1, where the measured round-turn spread is 5% to 57% of ATR (mean 19.0%). Nothing has ever gone UP the timeframe. Measured just now on the same caches: the same cost is 4.18% of ATR at D1 and 1.19% at W1 - a 5.3x and 16x reduction. Every candidate this project has killed died on cost, and the one lever that moves cost by an order of magnitude has never been pulled. Separately, this is the first hypothesis here that comes from OUTSIDE the data: time-series momentum (Moskowitz/Ooi/Pedersen 2012, 58 futures 1965-2009; extended to 1880 by Hurst/Ooi/Pedersen) is the most replicated anomaly in this space, and its prediction is made before the run rather than found by searching this sample.
entries.change: Resample H1 bid/ask to D1 for 10 markets, 2004-2026. At each month end take the sign of the trailing k-month mid-close return, k in {1,3,6,12}. Enter at the OPEN of the first trading day of the next month (ask for long, bid for short) and exit at the CLOSE of its last trading day (bid for long, ask for short). Non-overlapping monthly holds. Size to constant ex-ante volatility using an exponentially-weighted daily vol estimated only from data up to the signal, so R = realised return / ex-ante monthly vol. Decompose per market: raw E(R) = mean(d*x), drift term = mean(d)*mean(x), skill = covariance(d,x) - the genuine timing component. Build the equal-weight cross-market portfolio month by month so the pooled t accounts for cross-market correlation rather than assuming 10 independent tests. Swap = 0 in the main test per this project's cost rules, with a separate overnight report using the known XAUUSDc swap of -534.9 points.
entries.criterion: At the 12-month lookback - the literature's headline specification, fixed before the run - drift-adjusted skill positive on at least 8 of 10 markets AND the equal-weight portfolio's net-of-cost t clearing the multiple-testing floor.
entries.test_period: 10 markets D1 2004-2026 (XAUUSD, XAGUSD, USDSEK, EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD, NZDUSD). No entry rule in this repo was ever fitted at D1 or on a monthly hold, so the whole timeframe is out of sample with respect to every prior search here.

result.note: DOES NOT CLEAR. At the headline 12-month lookback the equal-weight portfolio makes +0.0248R/month, t +0.74, annualised Sharpe +0.13, and drift-adjusted skill is positive on 6 of 10 markets (binomial P 0.377, itself an upper bound since seven share the dollar). Declared bar was 8 of 10 plus a portfolio t clearing 3.66; both fail. The sweep is monotone in the literature's own direction (1m -0.0458 t -3.01, 3m -0.0439, 6m -0.0121, 12m +0.0248) - short-horizon reversal, long-horizon momentum - so the SIGN structure replicates while the magnitude does not survive this floor. Gold is again mostly drift: raw +0.2028 (t +2.29) splits into drift +0.1295 and skill +0.0852 (t +0.96), the same shape as Setup D. TWO FINDINGS THAT OUTLIVE THIS TEST. First, the cost premise was half right and half backwards: spread does collapse at D1 (gold 0.0119R/trade) but swap explodes (0.2498R/trade, 21x the spread), taking gold from +0.2028R to -0.0470R. Going up the timeframe trades a small cost problem for a larger one. Second, and it is closed form: with spread S paid once and swap w paid per night against a move growing like sqrt(h), cost/move is minimised at h* = S/w, with volatility cancelling entirely. For XAUUSDc long that is 0.4540/0.5349 = 0.85 nights. The cost-optimal hold for a gold long on this account is under one night, which means the premise of this file was wrong before the first trade was simulated - and the H1/H4 horizons this project has always used are not a habit but close to the only viable window. The asymmetry is unexploited: a gold short receives financing, so h* does not exist on that side, and this repo has worked the long side throughout.
